source: RFC 0007 §10.3, Q22; RFC 0008 §3.2 (reviews of #996, #998); D2 (PIP-12 parity, review L5 of #1200)
statement: simulate, explain and analyze call the same Engine.evaluate as enforcement, and explanations are built by the enforcing flow. simulate, explain and a shadow window's comparison decide on the documents enforcement reads, by its one rule (ViewDocuments): the platform's, the tenant's, and the app's when the scope has roles in that app or the tenant document decided with (the head, the candidate, or the revision explained) binds one of that app's permission policies to Anyone or a principal; never more. What explain reports as the revisions decided on, and the documents simulate takes a candidate of, are those the view read: a tenant document that does not compile makes a roleless request read no app document. A shadow window's candidate is decided with the failures of the documents it reads, and only those: a tenant candidate that no longer reads an app document is not indeterminate for that document's failure, and one that starts reading an app document that cannot be read or does not compile is (#1410). A candidate of a document that does not compile replaces that failure with itself; one of a document the view could not read is not compared (BASE_MISMATCH). A simulated or explained request that sends a header the documents of its view read with different values is refused 400, as enforcement refuses it before evaluation (PIP-12). An http resource goes through the path normalization every request's path does (PathNormalizer; RC1-41): a path enforcement answers 400 (a dot segment after one decoding, an empty segment, an encoded separator or a backslash (PIP-14), a malformed escape, over 2,048 characters as written or 256 per segment once decoded (PIP-5)) is refused 400, by the one function enforcement's checks use (PathNormalizer.enforceable), and the normalized path, its path parameters removed, is decided; a typed resource is held to the same length bounds, as written. analyze takes its resource the same way. analyze resolves a binding's policy as the engine does: a built-in control-plane policy from the engine's own statements (BuiltinPolicies.CONTROL), never counted opaque (#1401); a break-glass binding of cosec:root is listed as an allow marked break-glass, conditional on its window, with that window. An http action goes through the reading every request's method does (PIP-18), by the same function: a verb with a lower-case letter is refused 400, and http:HEAD is decided, and analyzed, as http:GET.
